title: Finite etale localization extension equals direct image
statement: Let $e:V\to X$ be a finite etale morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism], and let $R$ be any commutative ring. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], form the localization functor $L:V_{\mathrm{proet}}\to X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ by composition with $e$. Let $J_e$ be restriction of sheaves to presheaves, followed by left Kan extension along $L^{op}$, followed by sheafification. This is the usual slice extension construction [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization, def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. Then there is a natural isomorphism $J_e\cong e_*$ on sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image]. The coefficient ring need not be finite and the fibres may be empty.

source.place: Proof, first two paragraphs, ending before passage to complexes; the finite sum/product argument for the sheaf-level adjunction.

proof.text: An etale map is flat and unramified [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-unramified-morphism], so its diagonal is an open immersion. An open immersion induces isomorphisms on local rings [def-weil-open-immersion], hence is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Thus an etale map is flat with flat diagonal, i.e. weakly etale [def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism]. In particular $e$ is an object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], its slice site is $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and the restricted constant ring is $A_V$. The inverse image $e^*$ is restriction to this slice: the direct-image formula [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] on a test object $W$ is $F(W\times_XV)$, the direct image for the localization morphism, and the inverse images of this morphism agree. Apply [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] with $\mathcal O=A_X$ and slice object $V$. Denote its exact left adjoint to $e^*$ by $J_e$ to distinguish slice extension by zero from the compact-support derived functor. Thus $J_e\dashv e^*$ and both $J_e,e^*$ are exact. For each point $x\in X$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split] gives an etale neighbourhood $U\to X$ on which $V_U=\coprod_{s\in S_U}U$, with $S_U$ finite. These neighbourhoods are jointly surjective. Their maps are flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism], and hence open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. Over each affine test open, cover their inverse images by affine opens; their images are open and cover the test open, so quasi-compactness selects finitely many. Together with weak etaleness this is precisely the covering criterion of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; the sheet count is allowed to vary with $U$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: local splitting and the slice-site interpretation

proof.text: Fix one splitting neighbourhood $U$ and write $S=S_U$. A test object $W\to V_U$ is covered by its disjoint inverse images $W_s$ of the sheets. The sheaf condition says $F(W)=\prod_s F(W_s)$, with zero value on an empty intersection. Thus a sheaf on $V_U$ is exactly a family $(F_s)_{s\in S}$ of module sheaves on $U$, and module maps are exactly families of module maps [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The direct-image formula [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] becomes $e_*F|_U=\prod_sF_s$ by applying that sheaf condition to $W\times_UV_U=\coprod_sW$. Restriction inverse image is the diagonal $N\mapsto(N)_s$ [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. The presheaf formula [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] and its sheafification in [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] give $J_eF|_U=\bigoplus_sF_s$: a map $W\to V_U$ is locally the inclusion of one sheet, so its generator is locally the corresponding summand generator, and restricting these generators gives exactly the restriction maps of that sum. Restriction to a slice uses the same covering families [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], so sheafification and this local description agree. For finitely many module sheaves this sum is also the sectionwise product: the coordinatewise module operations and restrictions satisfy the sheaf axiom, and the sum of finitely many coordinate maps has the coproduct universal property.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: finite tuple formulas, with sheaf condition and extension-by-zero construction expanded

proof.text: On this neighbourhood the canonical map $b:\bigoplus_sF_s\to\prod_tF_t$ has $(t,s)$-component $\operatorname{id}$ for $t=s$ and $0$ otherwise. Its inverse is $\sum_s\iota_s\pi_s$; composing in either order gives the identity by the finite coordinate calculation. For a change of splitting, refine the overlap into the open-and-closed inverse images of the sheets under the two splittings; on each such piece the change is a permutation. Relabelling $s,t$ preserves both the equality test $s=t$ in $b$ and the sum defining its inverse. Hence both local maps agree on overlaps. Apply [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] to $J_eF$ and $e_*F$ over $X$, and to the reversed pair, to glue $b$ and its inverse. The composites and naturality squares agree after the covering and therefore globally by uniqueness in that same lemma. This gives a natural isomorphism $J_e\cong e_*$. The claimed comparison is this natural isomorphism; no adjunction or derived-category assertion is part of the conclusion.

theorem finiteEtale_localizationExtensionIso {V X : Scheme.{u}} (e : V ⟶ X)
    [IsFinite e] [Etale e] (R : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing R] :
    Nonempty
      (Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback
          (MorphismProperty.Over.map ⊤ (inferInstance : WeaklyEtale e))
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R) (Scheme.ProEt.topology V) (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) ≅
        lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R) e)
